summary.headline: Belrise Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR27,464 million and PAT to INR1,663 million, with EBITDA margin at 12.0%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter by PAT, with manufacturing revenue up 26% YoY and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 13.5%. Management said cost pressures appear to be behind it and margins have returned to stable levels. The call focused on new wins: a first US smartphone-ecosystem fixtures order, a Dharwad CV chassis program, a three-wheeler body program, sheet metal entries with Japanese and European OEMs, and aerospace track-beam extensions at Chester Hall. Trading margins remain under pressure, and guidance of mid-teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins was maintained.

financial_highlights.value: 15.3%, excluding ~INR12,000 million unutilised QIP cash out of INR17,000 million
financial_highlights.change: ROCE 14.7% last year per management's Q2 remarks

segments.name: Manufacturing mix Q2 FY27
segments.commentary: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler 79.7%, PVs 5.4%, CVs 9.6%, others 5.3% of manufacturing revenue. Exports were 4.8% of manufacturing revenue (INR1,117 million).

segments.name: Manufacturing mix H1 FY27
segments.commentary: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler 80.5%, PVs 5.0%, CVs 9.1%, others 5.4% of manufacturing revenue. Exports were 4.6% (INR2,112 million).

segments.name: Aerospace (Chester Hall, UK)
segments.commentary: Management estimated aerospace at about 2.5%-3.5% of manufacturing revenue in Q2. Track-beam order extension for a large aircraft programme, with price increases; manufacturing currently happens only in the UK.

segments.name: Trading business
segments.commentary: Margins under pressure; management said the share of trading is falling intentionally and expects a return to normalcy over the next few quarters.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth guidance maintained, with stable EBITDA margins; no revision.
Aerospace and defence target of more than 10% of manufacturing revenue within 12-18 months, and upwards of 10% of revenue in the medium term; growth to be mix of organic and inorganic.
ROCE ambition of high teens over the next couple of years, driven by lower capex-to-revenue, better utilisation and proprietary products.
Dharwad CV chassis facility ramp-up in Q1 FY28, targeting INR1,500-2,000 million annual revenue at peak.
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar three-wheeler body facility ramp-up from Q1 FY28, targeting INR1,000-1,200 million annual revenue at peak.
Merger with Badve auto component business: NCLT application filed, expected 6-8 months; completion around end Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Dharwad: new facility for a leading CV OEM, manufacturing long members and complete chassis assemblies; ramp-up Q1 FY28; can make parts from 400 milligrams to 400 kilograms.
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: new facility for complete three-wheeler body and chassis; production line set up, ramp-up from Q1 FY28.
Suspension business: six OEMs onboarded; sixth OEM supplying from Q3 FY27; two further models from a South India OEM to start production in Q4 FY27.
Sheet metal wins: Greater Noida (Japanese PV OEM) and Pune (European PV OEM).
Chester Hall: AS9100 certification obtained for one facility; India aerospace manufacturing for the OEM expected to ramp over the next few quarters.
Around INR12,000 million of QIP proceeds remain unutilised; management expects deployment over the coming few quarters.
demand_pricing: Management said commodity price effects are small: mainly mild and stainless steel, which were less volatile than copper or aluminium. Most revenue growth attributed to volume and premium mix.
Customer breadth: all top 10 two-wheeler OEMs, and 12 of the top 15 PV and CV OEMs.

Electronics entry: first CNC fixtures order from a US smartphone OEM's ecosystem, after about 18 months of engagement; management cited a multi-hundred-million-dollar opportunity for this OEM alone. Order is modest but recurring, with fixture changes every few months.
Japanese PV OEM sheet metal order is its first in that OEM's sheet metal portfolio; high-tonnage parts described as higher margin. Initial order is small.
Yamato Co, Ltd licence (signed after quarter end): exclusive India rights for air filters, oil filters and resin air intake manifolds for automotive and industrial OEMs.
Management said trading margins are under pressure, with cost pressures largely behind it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term revenue target from aerospace and defence, and when will it contribute meaningfully to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Upwards of 10% of revenue from aerospace and defence in the medium term. Management said the segment will be EBITDA-margin and ROCE accretive once revenue comes through, using a UK/Europe hub with India as the cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and scaling path of the consumer electronics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the initial order is modest and the business is only a few weeks old. The product cycle runs about 8-9 months after starting in a couple of months, and talks cover MLB and FATP fixtures. No long-term aspiration was given yet.

qa_highlights.question: Can the aerospace track-beam order be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify it. It said the programme runs for at least the next half decade with volume and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Badve auto merger complete, and what is the trading business outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: NCLT application filed; 6-8 month timeline, around end Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28. Trading margins are under pressure and expected to normalise over the next few quarters. Management gave no comment on hiving off trading into a separate entity.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any guidance revision, and what is aerospace's share of Q2 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No revision to mid-teens revenue growth. Aerospace was estimated at about 2.5%-3.5% of manufacturing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the auto growth came from commodity prices versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most growth came from volume and premium segments; commodity pass-through was a very small portion.

risks_watch: Trading business margins remain under pressure; management expects normalisation only over the next few quarters.
Aerospace contribution is still small (about 2.5%-3.5%); the 10%+ target depends on wins and possibly inorganic steps.
Electronics order is small and its scale is unproven; the first product cycle must run before the business can compound.
Dharwad, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and suspension ramp-ups (Q4 FY27 to Q1 FY28) need to meet timelines.
About INR12,000 million of unutilised QIP proceeds weighs on reported ROCE until deployed.
Merger timing depends on NCLT approval; management declined to comment on hiving off the trading business.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order wins and margin stability, with some caution on trading margins. Management gave no quantification of the track-beam order and no long-term electronics target, and said the trading business outlook is only a return to normal over the next few quarters.
key_quotes: Against a backdrop of continued uncertainty, we delivered our strongest quarter ever, with PAT reaching INR1,663 million.
Last quarter, we had indicated that the worst of the cost pressures were behind us, and we are pleased to report a return to stable margins this quarter.
So, we feel we need to learn how to crawl first, and then walk, and then run.
We have applied to the NCLT for that.
